texts.preamble: Delhi Golf Club Employees Union vs Union Of India on 24 February, 2022 Author: Vipin Sanghi Bench: Vipin Sanghi, Jasmeet Singh $~4. * In The High Court Of Delhi At New Delhi + Lpa 239/2021 and C.M. Nos.25446-25449/2021 & 9922/2022 Delhi Golf Club Employees Union ..... Through: Mr. Inderbir Singh Alag Advocate with Mr. Simra & Ms. Rhea Dube, Advoca versus Union Of India .....
texts.arguments: The submission of Mr. Alag, learned counsel for the appellant is that while passing the impugned judgment, the learned Single Judge has not completely dealt with the petitioners' submission advanced in W.P.(C.) No.5440/2020. The learned Single Judge has - in paragraph 5 of the impugned judgment, recorded in relation to the W.P.(C.) No.5440/2020 as follows: "5. Multiple directions are sought in the petition against Union of India, Special/Additional/Joint Labour Commissioners, Delhi Advisory Contract Labour Board and other concerned Departments including DGC to prohibit deployment of contract labour by DGC and to forward the application of the Petitioners under Section 10 of the Contract Labour (Regulation & Abolition) Act, 1970 to the State Advisory Contract Labour Board for prohibition of deployment of contract labour in the Food and Beverages Department of DGC under Section 4 of the said Act. Directions are also sought to Respondent Nos. 7 and 8 to initiate action against the concerned Labour Commissioners for contravening their statutory duties and a direction to Respondent No.4 not to grant Principal Employer Registration Delhi Golf Club Employees Union vs Union Of India on 24 February, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159134711/ 1 Certificate to the Management of DGC and to cancel the same, if already granted. Any other Writ, Order or direction in the nature of MANDAMUS or any other appropriate writ, order or direction the Honble Court may deem fit and proper may also be granted in the facts and circumstances of the present case and in the interest of Justice."" 2. Mr. Alag submits that the case of the appellant in the said writ petition was that on 07.08.2020, the Conciliation Officer had passed an 'order' to the effect that retrenchment of 66 workmen was undertaken without compliance of Section 25N(7) and that the appellant workmen are deemed to be in the employment of the respondent/ Delhi Golf Club in the absence of permission from the Appropriate Government. Mr. Alag submits that it was in this light that W.P.(C.) No.5440/2020 was filed to seek the reliefs, as set out in the aforesaid extract. 3. The said position taken by the appellant was seriously contested by the respondents, who claimed that the file noting dated 07.08.2020 made by the Conciliation Officer was not an 'order' and the Conciliation Officer had no authority, or jurisdiction to pass any order. Several other pleas were also raised by the respondent. The Labour Department had also filed an affidavit stating that the Delhi Golf Club Employees Union vs Union Of India on 24 February, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159134711/ 3 proceedings dated 07.08.2020 undertaken by the Conciliation Officer was not an 'order'. It was contended by the respondent that the said writ petition itself was not maintainable.
